hypothesis.title: The Thread That Survives
hypothesis.question: Across audio compression, watermarking, speech synthesis alignment, harmonic geometry, and studio production, what determines whether a transformed musical object is still heard as itself?
hypothesis.hypothesis: Musical identity survives transformation when the composer or system preserves a deliberately chosen invariant at the right representational layer: intelligibility, prosody, relational geometry, affective demo-energy, or surface timbre. Transformations fail when they optimize fidelity at one layer while breaking the layer that carries recognition or function.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: ClariCodec separates intelligibility from acoustic reconstruction, showing that low surface fidelity can preserve high message value (S4). StreamMark operationalizes identity as semi-fragility: robust under benign transformations but broken by semantic edits (S5). Qwen3.5-Omni/ARIA frames prosody as an alignment problem across token systems (S3). Tonnetz geometry preserves relational continuity rather than waveform detail (S6). David Mayer's demo-referencing practice supplies the studio analogue: keep returning to the early emotional invariant while adding layers and polish (S1). The HHL architecture adds a related caution: once a state is collapsed into blocks, the downstream chain depends on what was preserved at the measurement boundary (S2).

recipe.title: Semi-Fragile Variation Test
recipe.bodyMd: Choose a four-bar musical object and define three layers: semantic recognition, prosodic feel, and surface timbre. Make five transformations: aggressive codec degradation, graph-adjacent reharmonization, timing/prosody drift, timbral replacement, and one deliberate semantic attack. Compare where the listener stops hearing variation and starts hearing replacement. The test borrows intelligibility-vs-detail separation from S4, benign-vs-identity-altering transformations from S5, alignment sensitivity from S3, relational continuity from S6, and demo-energy preservation from S1.

parameters.value: listener recognition threshold across five transformations

dawChecklist: Bounce a rough demo/reference and keep it in the session as an identity anchor.
Create one heavily compressed/bitrate-reduced version while preserving contour and rhythm.
Create one reharmonized version constrained by close voice-leading or Tonnetz adjacency.
Create one timing-altered version that tests how far prosody can drift.
Create one timbre-swapped version that keeps rhythm and contour constant.
Create one deliberate semantic attack that breaks the named invariant.
A/B each against the demo and log which invariant actually carried recognition.

protocol.listeningContext: Studio monitoring or headphones; compare each transformed excerpt against the original demo/reference.
protocol.listeningMethod: Blind-shuffle transformed excerpts if possible, then label same/variation/replacement and note which musical feature carried the decision.
whatStaysConstant: nominal melodic/rhythmic material except in the semantic attack condition
